content:
anya: Heads-up: tracing shows prompt texts and user_ids are flowing into our OTLP pipeline. This is causing huge cardinality in the traces/exported attributes and bloating storage. We need a scrub/hand-off policy before the exporter.
sam: Agreed. We've started seeing prompt attribute cardinality spikes in prometheus labels and bigquery tables. Quick proposal: always redact full prompt, emit only a salted hash + length bucket. Keep user_id pseudonymized (HMAC), and remove ephemeral request IDs unless sampled.
mike: Can we do deterministic hashing so we can correlate across traces without storing PII? e.g. HMAC with tenant-specific salt. That still lets us dedupe.
anya: Yeah deterministic HMAC per-tenant is fine. But product will push back if we can't reproduce hallucination bugs (they want raw prompt occasionally).
jess: We do need the ability to see the exact prompt for high-severity bugs or legal requests. Can we gate raw prompt retention to: 1) explicit consent/enterprise config OR 2) low-sample-rate capture with strong audit logs?
sam: Proposal: default pipeline rules = scrub full prompt attribute, emit: prompt.hash (hmac-sha256 truncated), prompt.len (int), prompt.slice_bucket (e.g., "<64", "64-256", ">256"). For debugging, support a sampled "full_prompt_capture" flag that stores prompt.text for N% of requests for a tenant (configurable, default 0). Also keep a per-tenant HMAC salt for hashing.
anya: That sounds good. Need concrete processors for OpenTelemetry Collector. Sam, can you paste an example config we can test?
sam: Sure — example attribute processor to hash and scrub (OTEL collector config snippet):
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/title_hash:
    actions:
      - key: prompt
        action: update
        from_attribute: prompt
        # transform using a custom filter processor in our pipeline (see transform script)
  transform/scrub_prompt:
    statements:
      - set(attributes["prompt.hash"], string(hmac_sha256(env("TENANT_SALT"), attributes["prompt"])) )
      - set(attributes["prompt.len"], to_int(len(attributes["prompt"])))
      - set(attributes["prompt.size_bucket"], if(len(attributes["prompt"]) < 64, "<64", if(len(attributes["prompt"]) < 256, "64-256", ">=256")))
      - delete_key(attributes, "prompt")
```
(we'll implement hmac_sha256 as a small extension to the transform processor or run a sidecar that replaces it)
mike: We should also strip emails, IPs and credit-card-like strings before hashing to avoid weird collisions and PII in hashes. Regex scrub first, then HMAC.
sam: Good point. Order = 1) apply regex scrubs (email/ip/cc) -> 2) compute HMAC -> 3) delete original. Also keep a short snippet (first 40 chars) only for sampled traces to help triage.
jess: Sampling rules: console toggle + per-tenant config + a safe-rollout UX—product wants an explicit consent flow for enterprise: enable raw prompts -> show audit change log -> retention period.
anya: For exporters: OTLP -> bigquery and traces -> tempo/jaeger. We must ensure the exporters never get the unsanitized prompt. That means the collector must be the single ingress point for telemetry and the only place with access to the TENANT_SALT.
mike: Operationally, that implies the collector runs in our control plane and we don't forward raw spans from customer side without passing through the collector. For Private deployments we need a way to give customers a self-service config but ensure a review/approval for enabling raw capture.
sam: Also retention: hashed attributes can live longer (e.g., 90 days) but full text (sampled) must be 30 days and gated. We'll add data-retention metadata to trace resources so storage jobs can purge accordingly.
anya: Another ask: add a standard list of attributes we always scrub: prompt, user_email, user_id (unless pseudonymized), session_id, auth_token, cookie, device_fingerprint. Document it in the internal telemetry RFC.
mike: For correlation we do need a stable pseudonymous user key. We'll keep user.id as user.id.pseudonym (HMAC) and keep a lookup only in a secure store for legal/enterprise requests, with audit logs for access.
jess: UX: In console for rollouts, surface a "Telemetry Data Exposure" card when enabling any raw capture. Show retention, sample rate, and last audit. Also require an owner and an expiry date.
anya: Action items: 1) Sam to PR OTEL processor + unit tests for regex scrub -> hmac -> delete (due EOD). 2) Mike to draft deployment model for collectors (hosted vs private) and review KMS for TENANT_SALT (due Wed). 3) Jess to write product-facing consent and console UI copy + audit flow (due Fri). 4) I'll add the retention policy rows to the telemetry RFC.
sam: I'll include a small Python example for computing the hash so SDKs can replicate for client-side sampling decisions:
```python
import hmac, hashlib


def prompt_hash(salt: str, prompt: str) -> str:
    return hmac.new(salt.encode(), prompt.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16]
```
(we truncate to 16 hex chars to keep attribute size small but still low collision).
mike: One more thing — request_id. Right now request_id in logs is raw and used for tracing. We should keep trace_id and make request_id optional: store request_id.hash only in traces, keep raw only in ephemeral logging layer (retention 7 days) for debugging. That prevents long-lived analytics joins creating cardinality.
anya: Sounds agreed. If there are no objections I'll merge the RFC changes and we can start a canary for a single tenant with sampled full prompts in staging.
jess: lgtm from product side. :thumbsup:
otel-bot: Reminder: please add an OTEL-processor integration test to ensure prompt attribute is removed before exporter (ticket #TELEMETRY-412).
anya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the RFC PR for exact wording.
